pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 50 KB
pages.description: Shrink a one-page PDF to under 50 KB for strict form uploads like marksheets and certificates. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Some portals cap each document at 50 KB. A single page made from text fits easily; a single scanned page usually can too.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 50 KB
paragraphs: 50 KB is about the smallest limit you will see for a PDF, and it is realistic for one page. A page exported from Word or a web form is mostly text and is often already under it after the lossless cleanup.

A scanned page is a photo, so it has to shrink. We lower its resolution step by step, as far as 50 dpi for color and 100 dpi for black and white, and keep the first step that fits. Several scanned pages at 50 KB will usually hit that floor, and then you get the smallest file we could make with a note saying so.
tips: Upload one page per file. At this size every extra scanned page makes the rest blurrier.
Scan certificates and marksheets in black and white if the form accepts it. It is far smaller than color at the same sharpness.
If the scan is a phone photo, crop away the table or desk around the paper first.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 100 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 100 KB for exam, admission and government forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Exam and admission forms often cap certificates and ID scans at 100 KB. Scanned pages are mostly image data, so they usually get there with text still readable.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 100 KB
paragraphs: 100 KB is tight, but it depends on what is in the file. A PDF made straight from a document, exported from Word or a web form, is mostly text, and text takes almost no space. Those usually fit after the lossless pass alone. Scanned pages are photos of paper, and those are what have to shrink.

For scans we lower the resolution of the page images one step at a time, down to 50 dpi at the lowest setting, and stop at the first step that fits. Anything drawn as real text stays sharp at every step; only images lose detail.
tips: Scan one page per file if the form allows it. Every scanned page adds to the size.
Scan in grayscale or black and white when color does not matter. It compresses far better than color.
Crop the scan to the edge of the document. A strip of scanner lid still costs bytes.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 150 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 150 KB for scholarship, admission and registration forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 150 KB is a common cap for certificates and ID proofs on registration portals. Two or three scanned pages usually fit.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 150 KB
paragraphs: Registration and scholarship portals often allow 150 KB per document: an ID proof, a caste or income certificate, a fee receipt. Two or three scanned pages usually fit with the text still easy to read.

We run a lossless cleanup first, then step the page images down in resolution and JPEG quality together until the file is under 150,000 bytes. We stop at the first step that fits, so nothing is squeezed harder than it needs to be.
tips: Front and back of an ID card fit comfortably on one page. Put them side by side before scanning.
Check stamps, seals and signatures in the result. Fine, faint marks are the first thing to blur.
If the portal asks for a PDF but you have a photo, convert it to PDF first, then compress it here.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 200 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 200 KB for visa, ID and application uploads. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 200 KB is a common limit on visa and ID document uploads. A one or two page scan usually fits with room to spare.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 200 KB
paragraphs: Visa and ID portals often ask for a passport page, a bank statement or a photo ID under 200 KB. A one or two page scan usually gets there at a resolution that is still easy to read.

We try a lossless cleanup first. If the file is still too big, we step the page images down in resolution and JPEG quality together and keep the gentlest step that fits under 200,000 bytes, so it passes however the portal counts a kilobyte.
tips: Zoom in on the result before you upload. Small print like passport numbers and dates is what suffers first.
If a long statement will not fit, check whether the portal only needs the pages it asks for.
Filling in a form PDF? Fill it and save it first. The stronger settings can flatten fillable fields.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 300 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 300 KB for online application portals. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 300 KB leaves enough room for a few scanned pages at a size that is still comfortable to read on screen.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 300 KB
paragraphs: At 300 KB there is room for a few scanned pages at a resolution that reads comfortably on screen, or a much longer document if it was created digitally.

Digital PDFs mostly shrink in the lossless pass: we repack the file's internal structure and drop parts nothing uses, without changing how anything looks. Scans shrink by lowering image resolution a step at a time until the file fits.
tips: Include only the pages you need. Each extra scanned page counts against the limit.
If you can rescan, 150 to 200 dpi is plenty for reading on screen and leaves far less to compress away than 600 dpi.
If a file cannot reach 300 KB, you get the smallest version we could make and a note saying so.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 400 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 400 KB for application and document verification portals. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 400 KB leaves room for several scanned pages at a comfortable resolution, which is what most verification portals need.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 400 KB
paragraphs: At 400 KB a short scanned document, like a four or five page transcript or a lease, usually fits at around 100 to 150 dpi. That is sharp enough to read small print on screen.

Documents with photos or colored backgrounds are the harder case, because every page is a full-color image. Those step down further, and the result is the gentlest setting that still fits under 400,000 bytes.
tips: Remove blank pages, including the backs of single-sided sheets that a duplex scanner picked up.
A document created on a computer, rather than scanned, is often already far under 400 KB. Try the original file before a scan of a printout.
Zoom in to 100% on the result and read one line of small print before you upload it.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 500 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 500 KB for applications, certificates and forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 500 KB fits most multi-page scans, like transcripts or a set of certificates, without the pages turning blurry.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 500 KB
paragraphs: 500 KB fits most multi-page documents: transcripts, a set of certificates, a signed contract. Pages usually stay close to print quality.
Our highest-quality settings keep color images at 200 to 300 dpi. We only go lower when the file still does not fit, and we always stop at the first setting that does.
tips: Photos embedded in a document are usually most of its size. Text and tables add very little.
Keep your original for printing. The compressed copy is meant for uploading.
Password-protected PDFs cannot be compressed. Remove the password first, then upload.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 1 MB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 1 MB for job applications and resume uploads. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Job sites and applicant tracking systems often limit resumes and cover letters to 1 MB. Text-heavy PDFs usually fit without visible change.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 1 MB
paragraphs: Job sites and applicant tracking systems often cap resumes, cover letters and portfolios at 1 MB. A resume exported from Word or Google Docs is usually well under that already. Oversized ones are almost always carrying a large photo or come from a design tool.
Text and vector graphics stay sharp at every setting. Only embedded images are resampled, so a headshot or logo gets smaller while your text stays crisp.
tips: PDFs exported from design tools often embed images at full resolution, which is exactly what we reduce.
Keep your text as real text rather than a scanned image, so applicant tracking systems can read it.
The download is named yourfile.fit.pdf. Rename it to something like firstname-lastname-resume.pdf before you apply.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 2 MB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 2 MB for upload forms and portals. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 2 MB is a common ceiling on upload forms. Photos inside the PDF get resized just enough to fit and no further.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 2 MB
paragraphs: 2 MB is a common ceiling on upload forms, insurance claims and school portals. Photo-heavy PDFs and long scans are the usual reasons a file goes over.
We reduce the photos inside the PDF only as far as needed. The first setting keeps images at 300 dpi and high JPEG quality, and the search stops at the first setting that fits.
tips: Phone photos dropped into a document can be several megabytes each on their own.
If the form accepts more than one file, splitting a long document keeps each part sharper.
The original is deleted 5 minutes after the run finishes, so try other sizes before then.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 5 MB
pages.description: Shrink a large PDF to under 5 MB for email attachments and portals. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: For big scans and photo-heavy reports that need to go through email or a portal with a 5 MB cap.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 5 MB
paragraphs: 5 MB covers most email attachments and portals with a larger limit. Big scans, photo reports and slide decks saved as PDF are the files that usually need it.
At this size most files keep high-resolution images. Very large ones, like dozens of scanned pages or print-resolution artwork, may still need the stronger settings.
tips: Uploads can be up to 50 MB. Split anything larger before you start.
Big files take longer, since each setting is a full pass over the document. A large scan can take a minute or two.
Keep your original. The compressed copy is for sending, not for printing or editing.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 10 MB
pages.description: Shrink a large PDF to under 10 MB for email, court filings and grant or tender portals. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: For long scans, portfolios and reports that need to get under a 10 MB email or portal limit without losing print quality.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 10 MB
paragraphs: 10 MB is the limit for many email systems, e-filing portals and grant or tender submissions. The files that need it are usually long scans, design portfolios or reports full of photos.

At this size most documents keep images at 200 to 300 dpi, which still prints well. Often the lossless pass alone gets there, since PDFs exported from design tools tend to carry duplicate fonts and uncompressed data.
tips: Uploads can be up to 50 MB. Split anything larger into parts first.
Some mail servers count an attachment after encoding, which makes it about a third bigger. If a 10 MB mail limit rejects the file, try a 7 MB target.
Large files take longer, since each setting is a full pass over the document. Leave the tab open until it finishes.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 20 KB
pages.description: Shrink a signature or photo to under 20 KB for online application forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Signature uploads on application forms are often capped at 10 to 20 KB. A signature on a plain background compresses very well.

guide.title: Getting a signature or small image under 20 KB
paragraphs: Application forms often want a scanned signature between 10 and 20 KB. A signature is dark ink on a plain background, which compresses very well once the image is a sensible size.
We shrink the pixel dimensions and JPEG quality together, down to 800 pixels on the longest side at the smallest setting, and keep the gentlest step that fits under 20,000 bytes.
tips: Sign in dark ink on plain white paper, and crop tightly around the signature before uploading.
Take the photo in good light so the paper comes out white rather than gray. A clean background takes far fewer bytes.
If the form also asks for exact pixel dimensions, check them. We shrink to hit the file size, not to a specific width and height.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 50 KB
pages.description: Shrink a passport-style photo to under 50 KB for application forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Photo uploads on application forms are often limited to 50 KB. A phone photo gets resized and re-encoded until it fits.

guide.title: Getting a photo under 50 KB
paragraphs: Photo uploads for exam registrations, applications and ID cards are often limited to 50 KB. A phone photo is usually several megabytes, so it has to lose most of its pixels.
We scale the photo down and lower JPEG quality together until it fits. Even the smallest setting keeps 800 pixels on the longest side, which is more than most photo forms display.
tips: Crop to head and shoulders before uploading. Fewer pixels to start with means less detail has to go.
Use a plain, light background. It takes far fewer bytes than a busy one.
If the form also has a minimum size or exact pixel dimensions, check the result against them. We aim for the file size only.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 100 KB
pages.description: Shrink a JPG, PNG or photo to under 100 KB. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 100 KB keeps a photo sharp enough for a profile picture or an ID upload.

guide.title: Getting an image under 100 KB
paragraphs: 100 KB is enough for a clear profile picture, an ID photo or a photo of a document for most online forms.
For a JPEG we first try an optimized re-encode that keeps every pixel exactly as it is. If that is not enough, we reduce the dimensions and quality step by step until it fits.
tips: A PNG comes back as a PNG, with its transparency kept.
Photographing a document? Shoot it flat and in good light, filling the frame. Less background means more detail survives.
We keep your image's shape and never crop it, so crop first if the form wants a particular framing.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 150 KB
pages.description: Shrink a photo to under 150 KB for profile pictures, ID uploads and online forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 150 KB is plenty for a clear profile or ID photo. A phone photo gets resized and re-encoded until it fits.

guide.title: Getting a photo under 150 KB
paragraphs: Profile pictures, student and employee ID uploads, and many online forms cap photos at 150 KB. That is enough for a clear, sharp picture at the size these sites display it.
We resize and re-encode in steps, from 4000 pixels on the longest side down to 800, and keep the largest, highest-quality step that fits under 150,000 bytes.
tips: Crop to the part of the photo that matters first. Every pixel you remove is one less that has to be squeezed.
Photos with lots of fine detail, like foliage or patterned clothes, take more bytes than a plain background.
A JPEG comes back as a JPEG and a PNG as a PNG, so the file type the form asked for is kept.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 200 KB
pages.description: Shrink a photo or scanned image to under 200 KB. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 200 KB is enough for a clear photo of a document or a good-quality portrait.

guide.title: Getting an image under 200 KB
paragraphs: 200 KB leaves room for a sharp portrait, a readable photo of a certificate or a product image for a listing.
We stop at the first setting that fits, so an image that only needs a little squeezing keeps most of its resolution and detail.
tips: iPhone photos (HEIC) work too. HEIC photos are saved as JPEG.
We remove camera metadata such as GPS location. It saves space and keeps where you took the photo private.
Every file comes back in the format you uploaded: a PNG stays a PNG, a WebP a WebP.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 300 KB
pages.description: Shrink a photo or scanned document image to under 300 KB for application portals. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 300 KB is a common cap for document photos on application portals. Text in a photographed page stays readable at this size.

guide.title: Getting an image under 300 KB
paragraphs: Many portals ask for a photo of a document, like an ID card, a utility bill or a receipt, under 300 KB. At this size a photographed page usually keeps 1600 pixels or more on its longest side, which keeps printed text readable.
We first try an optimised re-encode that leaves the pixels untouched. If that is not enough, we lower dimensions and JPEG quality together and stop at the first step that fits.
tips: Photograph documents flat, from straight above, in daylight. Shadows and a tilted page cost bytes and readability.
Crop out the background around the document before uploading.
Screenshots saved as PNG often drop far below 300 KB once converted, since PNG stores every pixel without lossy compression.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 500 KB
pages.description: Shrink a large phone photo to under 500 KB without it looking compressed. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Phone photos are often 3 to 5 MB. At 500 KB they still look good on any screen.

guide.title: Getting an image under 500 KB
paragraphs: Phone photos are often 3 to 5 MB. At 500 KB they still look good on any screen, which is why it is a common limit for listings, profile uploads and support forms.
Our highest-quality setting keeps up to 4000 pixels on the longest side at JPEG quality 92. We only step down as far as the size requires.
tips: Most screens show far fewer pixels than a phone camera captures, so the size drop is rarely visible.
Large PNG screenshots often shrink the most, since they are stored without lossy compression.
Need several photos done? Each file is compressed separately; upload them one at a time.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 1 MB
pages.description: Shrink a high-resolution photo to under 1 MB for listings, portfolios and support forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Modern phone and camera photos are often 5 MB or more. Under 1 MB they still look sharp full screen.

guide.title: Getting a photo under 1 MB
paragraphs: A photo from a recent phone or camera is often 5 to 12 MB. Marketplaces, rental listings, portfolio sites and support forms commonly cap uploads at 1 MB.

At 1 MB most photos keep 3000 pixels or more on the longest side at high JPEG quality, which is sharper than nearly any screen can show. Often the lossless re-encode, which only strips metadata, is enough on its own.
tips: Stripping metadata also removes the photo's GPS location, which is worth doing before you post it publicly.
iPhone photos (HEIC) work too. HEIC photos are saved as JPEG.
RAW files are not supported. Export a JPEG from your editor, then compress that.

pages.heading: Compress a PNG to 100 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PNG screenshot, logo or scan to under 100 KB. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: PNGs are stored without lossy compression, so screenshots and scans are often ten times bigger than they need to be.

guide.title: Getting a PNG under 100 KB
paragraphs: PNG keeps every pixel exactly, which is why a single screenshot or scanned page saved as PNG can be several megabytes. The result here stays a PNG: we reduce it to 256 colours, which screenshots, logos and diagrams barely show, and make it smaller in pixels only as far as 100 KB needs.
We try it at full size first, then step the pixel dimensions down, keeping the largest PNG that fits under 100,000 bytes. Transparent areas stay transparent.
tips: Logos keep their transparency, so they still work on a coloured background.
Crop screenshots to the part you need. A full-screen capture of a 4K display is a lot of pixels to squeeze.
A photo saved as PNG has too many colours to shrink well this way. If the form accepts JPEG, save the photo as a JPEG first; photos get much smaller that way.

pages.heading: Compress a PNG to 500 KB
pages.description: Shrink a large PNG, like a screenshot or design export, to under 500 KB. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Design exports and full-screen screenshots saved as PNG are often 3 to 10 MB. Reduced to 256 colours they usually fit under 500 KB, still a PNG and still sharp.

guide.title: Getting a PNG under 500 KB
paragraphs: A design export or a high-resolution screenshot saved as PNG is often 3 to 10 MB, because PNG never throws detail away. Most of that is colour precision nobody sees: reduced to 256 colours, the same image usually drops under 500 KB and stays a PNG, with text as sharp as before.
We try it at full size first and make it smaller in pixels only if 500 KB needs that. Transparent areas stay transparent.
tips: Zoom in on small text in the result before you upload it, in case the image had to be made smaller in pixels to fit.
For a photo, export a JPEG from your design tool instead: photos shrink much better as JPEG than as PNG.
Images with large flat areas of one color, like diagrams, shrink the most.

pages.heading: Convert HEIC to JPG
pages.description: Convert an iPhone HEIC photo to JPG, and fit it under a size limit if you need one. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: iPhones save photos as HEIC. The US visa form (DS-160), UK passport photos and Canadian immigration uploads accept JPEG, not HEIC.

guide.title: Turning an iPhone photo into a JPG
paragraphs: iPhones save photos as HEIC to use less space. The US visa form (DS-160), UK passport photos and Canadian immigration uploads all ask for JPEG, and Windows needs a paid extension just to open a HEIC.

We convert it to a JPG, turned the right way up, with its colours converted to the standard sRGB every site expects, and keep every pixel when the limit allows. A JPG of the same photo is usually about twice the size of the HEIC, so if the form has a limit, pick it below and we fit the JPG under it in the same step.
tips: On an iPhone, uploading straight from Safari usually hands the site a JPG already. This is for HEIC files that have reached a computer, by AirDrop, iCloud or email.
To stop your iPhone saving HEIC at all, go to Settings, Camera, Formats and choose Most Compatible.
We remove camera metadata such as GPS location from the JPG, which also keeps where you took the photo private.

pages.heading: Convert HEIC to JPG under 1 MB
pages.description: Turn an iPhone HEIC photo into a JPG under 1 MB, in one step. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: An iPhone photo converted to JPG is often 3 to 6 MB. 1 MB still keeps plenty of detail.

guide.title: Getting an iPhone photo under 1 MB as a JPG
paragraphs: Converting a HEIC to JPG roughly doubles its size, so a photo that was 2 MB on your phone can land at 4 MB or more, over a 1 MB upload limit.

We convert and shrink in one step, keeping the most resolution that fits. A 12-megapixel iPhone photo under 1 MB usually keeps around 2,600 pixels on its long side, plenty for a form, a listing or a profile.
tips: On an iPhone, uploading straight from Safari usually hands the site a JPG already. This is for HEIC files that have reached a computer, by AirDrop, iCloud or email.
If the form also asks for exact pixel dimensions, open Exact size in pixels before you compress.
We remove camera metadata such as GPS location from the JPG, which also keeps where you took the photo private.

pages.heading: Convert HEIC to JPG under 200 KB
pages.description: Turn an iPhone HEIC photo into a JPG under 200 KB for an application form. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 200 KB is a common limit for photos on visa, exam and job application forms, which usually ask for JPEG.

guide.title: An iPhone photo as a JPG under 200 KB
paragraphs: Application forms that cap photos at 200 KB almost always want JPG too. Uploading the HEIC straight from a computer fails twice: wrong format, and several times too big.
We fix both at once. A 12-megapixel iPhone photo under 200 KB usually keeps around 1,800 pixels on its long side, still sharp for a portrait or a photo of a document.
tips: If the form gives exact pixel dimensions, like 600 x 600 for a US visa photo, open Exact size in pixels and enter them; we crop to fill.
On an iPhone, uploading straight from Safari usually hands the site a JPG already. This is for HEIC files that have reached a computer, by AirDrop, iCloud or email.
We remove camera metadata such as GPS location from the JPG, which also keeps where you took the photo private.

pages.heading: Convert HEIC to JPG under 100 KB
pages.description: Turn an iPhone HEIC photo into a JPG under 100 KB. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 100 KB is tight for an iPhone photo: converted to JPEG at full size, one is often several megabytes.

guide.title: An iPhone photo as a JPG under 100 KB
paragraphs: At 100 KB there is no room for a full iPhone photo, so the pixel size has to come down as well as the quality. We step both down together and keep the first setting that fits, so it stays as sharp as that size allows.
A 12-megapixel iPhone photo under 100 KB usually keeps around 1,600 pixels on its long side, clear on screen and fine for most form previews.
tips: Crop to what the form needs before you upload, such as your face for an ID photo. Fewer pixels to keep means more quality for the ones left.
On an iPhone, uploading straight from Safari usually hands the site a JPG already. This is for HEIC files that have reached a computer, by AirDrop, iCloud or email.
We remove camera metadata such as GPS location from the JPG, which also keeps where you took the photo private.

pages.heading: US visa photo for the DS-160: 600 x 600, under 240 KB
pages.title: US visa photo (DS-160)
pages.description: Make your DS-160 visa photo a 600 x 600 pixel JPEG under 240 KB, as the U.S. Department of State requires. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The DS-160 takes a square JPEG, 600 x 600 pixels and no more than 240 KB. A phone photo is several megabytes and the wrong shape, so it gets cropped, resized and compressed in one go.

source.label: the U.S. Department of State's photo requirements

guide.title: Getting a DS-160 photo to 600 x 600 and under 240 KB
paragraphs: The State Department sets four technical rules for the digital photo: JPEG format, 240 KB or less, a square shape, and 600 x 600 pixels. A file that misses any of them cannot be uploaded.

This page is set up for all four. Your photo is cropped to a square, where you place the crop box, scaled to exactly 600 x 600 pixels and saved as a JPEG at the highest quality that stays under 240 KB. At that size a photo usually fits with room to spare, so very little quality is lost.
tips: If your head is not in the middle of the photo, drag the crop box over it before you press Compress.
The picture itself has rules too, such as the background, your expression and glasses. Check them on the State Department page before you take it.
If the upload still complains, check that it is a JPEG. A PNG or HEIC from a phone is converted here, but a renamed file is not.

pages.heading: Indian e-Visa passport page: PDF under 300 KB
pages.title: Indian e-Visa passport page
pages.description: Compress the scanned bio page of your passport to a PDF under 300 KB for the Indian e-Visa application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The Indian e-Visa asks for the bio page of your passport as a PDF between 10 KB and 300 KB. A scan or phone photo of it is usually far bigger.

source.label: the Indian e-Visa site (Instructions for Applicant)

guide.title: Getting a passport page PDF under 300 KB
paragraphs: The e-Visa form takes the scanned bio page of your passport, the page with your photograph and details, as a PDF of at least 10 KB and at most 300 KB. Documents for a business or medical e-Visa have the same limits.

A single scanned page fits in 300 KB comfortably. We lower the resolution of the scan step by step and keep the first step that fits, so the text and your photo stay as sharp as the limit allows. The 10 KB minimum is never a problem for a real scan.
tips: Scan or photograph only the bio page, flat and in good light, with the whole page in the frame.
If your passport page is a JPG, save it as a PDF first (most phones can print to PDF), then compress it here.
Keep one page per file. The form asks for the bio page on its own.

pages.heading: Indian e-Visa photo: square JPEG under 1 MB
pages.title: Indian e-Visa photo
pages.description: Make your Indian e-Visa photo a square JPEG between 10 KB and 1 MB, as the e-Visa application requires. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The Indian e-Visa takes a JPEG photo between 10 KB and 1 MB whose height and width are equal. A phone photo is rarely square, so it is cropped to 1000 x 1000 pixels and compressed to fit.

source.label: the Indian e-Visa site (Instructions for Applicant)

guide.title: Getting an e-Visa photo square and under 1 MB
paragraphs: The e-Visa form asks for a JPEG of at least 10 KB and at most 1 MB, with equal height and width. It does not name a pixel size, so this page makes it 1000 x 1000: square, detailed, and comfortably under 1 MB.

The photo is cropped to a square where you place the crop box, resized, and saved at the highest JPEG quality that fits. You can change the pixel size in the options before you compress if you prefer another.
tips: If your face is not in the middle, drag the crop box over it before you press Compress.
The form also asks for a full face, front view, eyes open, without glasses, on a plain light background, with no shadows and no border.
A photo taken for a printed visa is fine to use; photograph or scan it in good light.

pages.heading: IBPS photo: 200 x 230 pixels, 20 KB to 50 KB
pages.title: IBPS photo
pages.description: Resize your photo to 200 x 230 pixels and 20 KB to 50 KB for IBPS bank exam applications. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: IBPS applications ask for a photo of 200 x 230 pixels and between 20 KB and 50 KB. A photo that small often comes out under 20 KB, so it is padded up to the minimum without changing the picture.

source.label: IBPS guidelines for scanning and uploading documents

guide.title: Getting an IBPS photo to 200 x 230 and 20 KB to 50 KB
paragraphs: IBPS guidelines ask for the photograph at 200 x 230 pixels with a file size between 20 KB and 50 KB. The minimum matters too: at 200 x 230 pixels a good-quality JPEG is often only 15 KB or so, and the form turns it away as too small.

Here the photo is cropped to 200 x 230 where you place the crop box, saved at the best quality under 50 KB, and if that comes out under 20 KB it is padded up to it. The padding is an invisible comment inside the file, so the picture is exactly the same.
tips: Recent IBPS notifications also ask for a live photo taken during registration, besides this upload. Check the notification for your exam.
Use a recent photo, face centred, on a light background. If your face is off to one side, drag the crop box over it.
Each recruitment publishes its own notification. If a form states a different size, set it in the options before you compress.

pages.heading: IBPS signature: 140 x 60 pixels, 10 KB to 20 KB
pages.title: IBPS signature
pages.description: Resize your signature to 140 x 60 pixels and 10 KB to 20 KB for IBPS bank exam applications. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: IBPS applications ask for a signature image of 140 x 60 pixels and between 10 KB and 20 KB. An image that small is only a few KB, so it is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

source.label: IBPS guidelines for scanning and uploading documents

guide.title: Getting an IBPS signature to 140 x 60 and 10 KB to 20 KB
paragraphs: IBPS guidelines ask for the signature at 140 x 60 pixels with a file size between 10 KB and 20 KB. A signature at 140 x 60 pixels is a tiny image, usually 3 to 5 KB even at the best quality, which is under the minimum and gets refused.

Here the signature is cropped to 140 x 60 where you place the crop box, saved at the best quality under 20 KB, and padded up to 10 KB with an invisible comment inside the file. The signature itself is exactly the same.
tips: Sign with a black pen on plain white paper, and photograph or scan it in good light.
Take the photo close around the signature, then drag the crop box so it keeps all of it.
Each recruitment publishes its own notification. If a form states a different size, set it in the options before you compress.

pages.heading: SBI photo: 200 x 230 pixels, 20 KB to 50 KB
pages.title: SBI photo
pages.description: Resize your photo to 200 x 230 pixels and 20 KB to 50 KB for SBI recruitment applications. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: SBI applications ask for a photo of 200 x 230 pixels and between 20 KB and 50 KB. A photo that small often comes out under 20 KB, so it is padded up to the minimum without changing the picture.

guide.title: Getting an SBI photo to 200 x 230 and 20 KB to 50 KB
paragraphs: SBI's recruitment notice asks for a recent passport-style colour photo, 200 x 230 pixels preferred, with a file size between 20 KB and 50 KB, as a JPG or JPEG.

Here the photo is cropped to 200 x 230 where you place the crop box, saved at the best quality under 50 KB, and if that comes out under 20 KB it is padded up to it with an invisible comment inside the file. The picture is exactly the same.
tips: Use a light, preferably white, background and look straight at the camera. Caps, hats and dark glasses are not accepted.
SBI also asks for a live photo taken with your webcam or phone during the application, besides this upload.
SBI publishes a notice for each recruitment. If yours states a different size, set it in the options before you compress.

pages.heading: SBI signature: 140 x 60 pixels, 10 KB to 20 KB
pages.title: SBI signature
pages.description: Resize your signature to 140 x 60 pixels and 10 KB to 20 KB for SBI recruitment applications. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: SBI applications ask for a signature of 140 x 60 pixels and between 10 KB and 20 KB. An image that small is only a few KB, so it is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

guide.title: Getting an SBI signature to 140 x 60 and 10 KB to 20 KB
paragraphs: SBI's recruitment notice asks for your signature in black ink on white paper, 140 x 60 pixels preferred, with a file size between 10 KB and 20 KB.

A signature at 140 x 60 pixels is usually 3 to 5 KB even at the best quality, which is under the minimum. Here it is cropped where you place the crop box, saved at the best quality under 20 KB and padded up to 10 KB with an invisible comment inside the file.
tips: Sign with a black pen on plain white paper, and photograph or scan it in good light.
Take the photo close around the signature, then drag the crop box so it keeps all of it.
SBI publishes a notice for each recruitment. If yours states a different size, set it in the options before you compress.

pages.heading: SBI left thumb impression: 240 x 240 pixels, 20 KB to 50 KB
pages.title: SBI left thumb impression
pages.description: Resize your left thumb impression to 240 x 240 pixels and 20 KB to 50 KB for SBI recruitment applications. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: SBI applications ask for a left thumb impression of 240 x 240 pixels and between 20 KB and 50 KB. It is cropped square, compressed, and padded up to 20 KB if it comes out smaller.

guide.title: Getting a thumb impression to 240 x 240 and 20 KB to 50 KB
paragraphs: SBI's recruitment notice asks for your left thumb impression in black or blue ink on white paper, 240 x 240 pixels preferred, with a file size between 20 KB and 50 KB, as a JPG or JPEG.

Here the image is cropped square where you place the crop box, resized to 240 x 240, saved at the best quality under 50 KB, and padded up to 20 KB with an invisible comment inside the file if it comes out smaller.
tips: Press the thumb once, firmly and evenly, so the ridges are clear rather than a smudge.
Photograph it straight on in good light and crop close around the print first, so the square crop keeps all of it.
If you do not have a left thumb, the notice allows your right thumb.

pages.heading: SBI handwritten declaration: 800 x 400 pixels, 50 KB to 100 KB
pages.title: SBI handwritten declaration
pages.description: Resize your handwritten declaration to 800 x 400 pixels and 50 KB to 100 KB for SBI recruitment applications. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: SBI applications ask for the handwritten declaration as an image of 800 x 400 pixels and between 50 KB and 100 KB. It is cropped, compressed, and padded up to 50 KB if it comes out smaller.

guide.title: Getting the declaration to 800 x 400 and 50 KB to 100 KB
paragraphs: SBI's recruitment notice asks you to write the declaration in English, in black ink on white paper, and upload it at 800 x 400 pixels preferred, with a file size between 50 KB and 100 KB, as a JPG or JPEG. The notice gives the exact wording to copy.

Here the photo of your page is cropped where you place the crop box to the 2 to 1 shape of 800 x 400, saved at the best quality under 100 KB, and padded up to 50 KB with an invisible comment inside the file if it comes out smaller.
tips: Write the declaration in your own handwriting, not in capital letters, and copy the wording from the notice exactly.
Take the photo close around the text, then drag the crop box so it keeps every line.
SBI publishes a notice for each recruitment. If yours states a different size, set it in the options before you compress.

pages.heading: RRB signature: 30 KB to 49 KB, at least 140 x 60 pixels
pages.title: RRB signature
pages.description: Resize your signature to 30 KB to 49 KB for Railway Recruitment Board applications (CEN 09/2025). Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: RRB's CEN 09/2025 asks for a signature JPEG between 30 KB and 49 KB, at least 140 x 60 pixels. A clean signature is far smaller than 30 KB, so it is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

guide.title: Getting an RRB signature to 30 KB to 49 KB
paragraphs: RRB's Centralised Employment Notification 09/2025 asks for a scanned signature, in running handwriting in black ink on white paper, as a JPG or JPEG between 30 KB and 49 KB and at least 140 x 60 pixels.

The form places the signature in a 35 x 20 mm box, so this page makes it 350 x 200 pixels, the same shape and well above the minimum. It is saved at the best quality under 49 KB, and because a signature at that size is usually well under 30 KB, it is padded up to 30 KB with an invisible comment inside the file. The signature is exactly the same.
tips: Sign in running (joined-up) handwriting. The notice rejects block, capital or disjointed letters.
Take the photo close around the signature, then drag the crop box so it keeps all of it.
Each notification sets its own rules. The RRB photo is captured live in the application, so there is no photo to upload.

pages.heading: RRB SC/ST certificate: PDF under 400 KB
pages.title: RRB SC/ST certificate
pages.description: Compress your SC/ST certificate to a PDF under 400 KB for the free travel pass on Railway Recruitment Board applications (CEN 09/2025). Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: RRB's CEN 09/2025 asks SC/ST candidates who want the free travel pass to upload their certificate as a PDF under 400 KB. A scan is often bigger, so it is compressed until it fits.

guide.title: Getting an SC/ST certificate PDF under 400 KB
paragraphs: RRB's Centralised Employment Notification 09/2025 asks SC/ST candidates who want the free railway travel pass to upload their SC/ST certificate as a PDF of less than 400 KB, legible and clear.
A certificate of one or two pages fits in 400 KB comfortably. We lower the resolution of the scan step by step and keep the first step that fits, so the text stays as readable as the limit allows.
tips: Scan the certificate flat and in good light, with the whole page in the frame.
If your certificate is a photo, save it as a PDF first (most phones can print to PDF), then compress it here.
The certificate must be the latest valid one as on the closing date of the application.

pages.heading: SSC signature for CGL and CHSL: 10 KB to 20 KB, about 6 x 2 cm
pages.title: SSC signature (CGL, CHSL)
pages.description: Resize your signature to a JPEG of 10 KB to 20 KB, about 6.0 x 2.0 cm, for SSC CGL and CHSL applications. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: SSC asks for a scanned signature as a JPEG between 10 KB and 20 KB, about 6.0 x 2.0 cm. A clean signature is often under 10 KB, so it is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

source.label: SSC's Combined Higher Secondary Level Examination 2026 notice

guide.title: Getting an SSC signature to 10 KB to 20 KB
paragraphs: The 2026 notices for the Combined Graduate Level (CGL) and Combined Higher Secondary Level (CHSL) examinations ask for a scanned signature in JPEG format, between 10 KB and 20 KB, about 6.0 cm wide and 2.0 cm high. They state that blurred or miniature signatures will be rejected.

This page makes the signature 600 x 200 pixels, the same 3 to 1 shape, cropped where you place the crop box. It is saved at the best quality under 20 KB, and if that comes out under 10 KB it is padded up to it with an invisible comment inside the file. The signature is exactly the same.
tips: Sign on plain white paper and take the photo close around the signature, so it fills the crop box.
Your photograph is not uploaded: SSC captures it live with your webcam or phone while you fill in the form.
Each SSC notice sets its own rules. If yours states a different size, set it in the options before you compress.

pages.heading: NEET UG photo: JPEG, 10 KB to 200 KB
pages.title: NEET (UG) photo
pages.description: Compress your passport-size photo to a JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB for the NEET (UG) application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The NEET (UG) form asks for a passport-size photograph as a JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB. A phone photo is usually several megabytes, so it is resized and compressed to fit.

guide.title: Getting a NEET photo under 200 KB
paragraphs: The NEET (UG) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for a recent passport-size photograph, in colour or black and white, as a JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB. 80% of the image should be your face, without a mask, with the ears visible, against a white background.
The bulletin sets no pixel size, so this page keeps the photo as large as fits under 200 KB, which leaves it sharp. It reduces the size step by step and stops at the first step that fits.
tips: Crop the photo close around your head and shoulders before you upload it, so your face fills most of the frame.
Use the same photo you will paste on the attendance sheet at the exam centre; the bulletin asks for the same one.
The form also takes a live photo with your webcam or phone. That one is not uploaded from a file.

pages.heading: NEET UG signature: JPEG, 10 KB to 100 KB
pages.title: NEET (UG) signature
pages.description: Compress your signature to a JPEG between 10 KB and 100 KB for the NEET (UG) application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The NEET (UG) form asks for your signature as a JPEG between 10 KB and 100 KB. A phone photo of it is far bigger, and a tightly cropped one can come out under 10 KB, so it is padded up to the minimum if needed.

guide.title: Getting a NEET signature to 10 KB to 100 KB
paragraphs: The NEET (UG) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for the signature file as a JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 100 KB, clearly legible. It sets no pixel size.
The image is kept as large as fits under 100 KB. If it comes out under 10 KB, it is padded up to the minimum with an invisible comment inside the file, so the signature itself is unchanged.
tips: Sign on plain white paper in dark ink and photograph it in good light, without shadows.
Crop close around the signature first, so it is not a small mark in a large white page.
There is no correction window for the signature, so check it is legible before you upload it.

pages.heading: NEET UG certificates: PDF, 50 KB to 300 KB
pages.title: NEET (UG) certificates and documents
pages.description: Compress your Class 10 certificate, category certificate or address proof to a PDF under 300 KB for the NEET (UG) application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The NEET (UG) form takes the Class 10 certificate, marksheet, category certificate, address proof and other documents as PDFs between 50 KB and 300 KB each. A scan is usually bigger.

guide.title: Getting a NEET document PDF under 300 KB
paragraphs: The NEET (UG) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for the Class 10 certificate and marksheet, the category certificate, the PwD or UDID certificate and the present and permanent address proofs as PDFs between 50 KB and 300 KB, clearly legible.

A one-page scan fits in 300 KB comfortably. We lower the resolution of the scan step by step and keep the first step that fits, so the text stays as sharp as the limit allows. A real scan is rarely under 50 KB; if yours is, scan it at a higher resolution.
tips: Make one PDF per document, as the form asks for each one separately.
If your document is a photo, save it as a PDF first (most phones can print to PDF), then compress it here.
Scan flat and in good light, with the whole page in the frame, so it stays legible at a small size.

pages.heading: JEE Main photo: JPEG, 10 KB to 200 KB
pages.title: JEE (Main) photo
pages.description: Compress your passport-size photo to a JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB for the JEE (Main) application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The JEE (Main) form asks for a colour passport-size photograph as a JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB. A phone photo is several megabytes, so it is resized and compressed to fit.

guide.title: Getting a JEE Main photo under 200 KB
paragraphs: The JEE (Main) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for a recent passport-size photograph in colour, with 80% of the face visible including the ears, without a mask, against a white background, as a JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB.
No pixel size is set, so the photo is kept as large as fits under 200 KB. Each step down is a little smaller, and the first one that fits is the one you get.
tips: Crop close around your head and shoulders first; the bulletin wants the face to fill most of the photo.
Keep your details on Aadhaar up to date. NTA matches your photos against them.
You also take a live photo during the application. That one comes from your webcam or phone, not from a file.

pages.heading: JEE Main signature: JPEG, 10 KB to 100 KB
pages.title: JEE (Main) signature
pages.description: Compress your signature to a JPEG between 10 KB and 100 KB for the JEE (Main) application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The JEE (Main) form asks for the signature as a JPEG between 10 KB and 100 KB. If a cropped signature comes out under 10 KB, it is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

guide.title: Getting a JEE Main signature to 10 KB to 100 KB
paragraphs: The JEE (Main) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for the signature file as a clearly legible JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 100 KB, with no pixel size given.

It is saved at the highest quality that fits under 100 KB. A small, clean signature can come out under 10 KB, and then it is padded up to 10 KB with an invisible comment inside the file. Nothing in the picture changes.
tips: Use a dark pen on white paper so the signature stays legible after compression.
Photograph it straight on, not at an angle, and crop away the rest of the page.
The same bulletin asks for the Class 10 certificate as a PDF of 50 KB to 300 KB. The NEET certificates page uses the same limits.

pages.heading: GATE 2027 photo: 3.5 x 4.5 cm JPEG under 600 KB
pages.title: GATE 2027 photo
pages.description: Crop your photo to passport size, 350 x 450 pixels, as a JPEG under 600 KB for the GATE 2027 application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: GATE 2027 takes a passport-size colour photo between 200 x 260 and 530 x 690 pixels, up to 600 KB. A phone photo is far bigger and the wrong shape, so it is cropped to 350 x 450 and saved as a JPEG.

guide.title: Getting a GATE photo to the right shape and size
paragraphs: The GATE 2027 Information Brochure asks for a colour passport-size photograph, 3.5 cm wide and 4.5 cm high, as a JPEG. Its width-to-height ratio must be between 0.66 and 0.89, it must be between 200 x 260 and 530 x 690 pixels, and the file can be up to 600 KB.

This page crops the photo to 350 x 450 pixels, the 3.5 to 4.5 shape and well inside both pixel limits, where you place the crop box. At that size a photo is far under 600 KB, so it is saved at high quality.
tips: Place the crop box so your face fills most of the frame: the brochure asks for the face to cover 60 to 70% of the image after cropping.
Use a plain white background, look straight at the camera, and avoid glare on glasses.
This photo appears on your admit card and score card, and a live photo is also taken during registration.

pages.heading: GATE 2027 signature: up to 580 x 180 pixels, under 300 KB
pages.title: GATE 2027 signature
pages.description: Crop your signature to 480 x 160 pixels, a JPEG under 300 KB, for the GATE 2027 application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: GATE 2027 takes a signature JPEG between 250 x 80 and 580 x 180 pixels, with a height to width ratio from 1:2.75 to 1:3.75, up to 300 KB. A photo of a signature is cropped to 480 x 160 to fit all three.

guide.title: Getting a GATE signature to the right shape
paragraphs: The GATE 2027 Information Brochure asks for the signature as a JPEG with a height to width ratio of 1 to between 2.75 and 3.75, between 250 x 80 and 580 x 180 pixels, and up to 300 KB. After cropping, the signature should cover 70 to 80% of the image.
This page crops it to 480 x 160 pixels, a ratio of 1 to 3, inside both pixel limits, where you place the crop box. A signature at that size is a small file, so it is saved at high quality.
tips: Sign in black or dark blue ink on white paper; the brochure accepts no other colours.
Drag the crop box tight around the signature so it fills most of the image.
Sign the way you will at the exam: a signature that does not match can lead to disqualification.

pages.heading: CUET UG photo: JPEG, 10 KB to 200 KB
pages.title: CUET (UG) photo
pages.description: Compress your passport-size photo to a JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB for the CUET (UG) application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The CUET (UG) form asks for a recent colour passport-size photo as a JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB. A phone photo is several megabytes, so it is resized and compressed until it fits.

guide.title: Getting a CUET photo under 200 KB
paragraphs: The CUET (UG) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for a scanned passport-size photograph in colour, with 80% of the face visible including the ears, without a mask, against a white background, as a JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB.
The bulletin gives no pixel size, so the photo stays as large as 200 KB allows. Each attempt is a little smaller than the last, and you get the first one that fits.
tips: Crop around your head and shoulders before uploading, so your face fills most of the photo.
Besides this upload, the form takes a live photo with your webcam or phone.
NTA checks photos against your Aadhaar details, so keep your Aadhaar photo recent.

pages.heading: CUET UG signature: JPEG, 10 KB to 50 KB
pages.title: CUET (UG) signature
pages.description: Compress your signature to a JPEG between 10 KB and 50 KB for the CUET (UG) application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The CUET (UG) form takes the signature as a JPEG between 10 KB and 50 KB, half the limit NEET and JEE Main allow. If it comes out under 10 KB, it is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

guide.title: Getting a CUET signature to 10 KB to 50 KB
paragraphs: The CUET (UG) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for the signature file as a clearly legible JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 50 KB. It gives no pixel size.

The signature is kept as large as fits under 50 KB. A small, clean one can come out under 10 KB, and then it is padded up to 10 KB with an invisible comment inside the file, so the image is unchanged.
tips: The CUET limit is 50 KB, lower than NEET and JEE Main, so a signature made for those may need compressing again.
Sign in dark ink on plain white paper and photograph it straight on, in good light.
Crop away the rest of the page so the signature fills the image.

pages.heading: IRCC document upload: PDF under 4 MB for Canadian immigration
pages.title: IRCC document upload
pages.description: Compress a scanned document to a PDF under 4 MB for IRCC: the secure account, Permanent Residence Portal, citizenship and asylum uploads. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Most IRCC accounts take files up to 4 MB, and the IRCC Portal up to 5 MB. A PDF under 4 MB uploads to any of them. Multi-page scans are usually far bigger.

source.label: the IRCC Help Centre's file size limits

guide.title: Getting an IRCC document under 4 MB
paragraphs: IRCC sets the limit per account: 4 MB for the IRCC secure account, the Permanent Residence Portal, the online citizenship application and the asylum portal, and 5 MB for the IRCC Portal. Aiming under 4 MB means the same file works wherever you upload it.

Each upload field takes one file, so a document with several pages, such as a passport or a set of bank statements, has to be a single PDF. Scanned at full quality that is often 10 to 30 MB. Here the scan's resolution is lowered step by step and the first step that fits is kept, so text stays as sharp as 4 MB allows.
tips: Combine all the pages into one PDF first. If you upload several files to one field, IRCC keeps only the last one.
Scanning at 150 to 300 DPI is plenty; higher only makes a bigger file to shrink.
Some IRCC forms set a lower limit, as low as 2 MB. If the upload page states one, choose that size instead.
This page is for documents. IRCC photos must be the photographer's original file, not altered in any way, so upload those as they are.

pages.heading: Discord emoji GIF: 128 x 128 under 256 KB
pages.title: Discord custom emoji
pages.description: Crop a GIF to 128 x 128 and fit it under 256 KB for a Discord custom emoji, still animated. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Discord takes custom emoji under 256 KB, at up to 128 x 128 pixels. A GIF from a phone or a GIF site is usually far bigger, so it is cropped to 128 x 128 and compressed until it fits, still animated.

source.label: Discord's help article on adding emojis

guide.title: Getting a GIF under Discord's emoji limit
paragraphs: Discord's help center says a custom emoji file must be smaller than 256 KB, and that emoji look best uploaded at up to 128 x 128 pixels, since they are shown at 32 x 32. Animated emoji are GIFs.

This page crops the GIF to 128 x 128 where you place the crop box, then compresses it to the largest file under 256 KB. Every frame keeps its timing, and the GIF still loops. If it cannot fit with every frame, some frames are dropped and the rest are held longer, so it plays at the same speed; the result says when that happened.
tips: Animated emoji use 50 extra slots that a server gets with Nitro or Nitro Basic.
Short loops fit best. A few seconds at 128 x 128 usually fits with every frame kept.
Choose Add a see-through border instead of cropping to keep the whole picture.

pages.heading: Discord banner GIF: 680 x 240 under 10 MB
pages.title: Discord profile banner
pages.description: Crop a GIF to 680 x 240 and fit it under 10 MB for a Discord profile banner, still animated. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Discord profile banners must be under 10 MB and at least 680 x 240 pixels. A GIF is cropped to exactly 680 x 240, the banner's shape, and compressed until it fits, still animated.

source.label: Discord's help article on custom profiles

guide.title: Getting a GIF under Discord's banner limit
paragraphs: Discord's help center says banners must be PNG, JPG or animated GIF files under 10 MB, at least 680 x 240 pixels. Only Nitro members can upload an image or GIF as their profile banner.

This page crops the GIF to 680 x 240 where you place the crop box, so Discord does not have to crop it again, then compresses it to the largest file under 10 MB. Every frame keeps its timing, and the GIF still loops. If it cannot fit with every frame, some frames are dropped and the rest are held longer, so it plays at the same speed; the result says when that happened.
tips: Place the crop box over the part that matters: a wide clip cut from a tall video loses its top and bottom.
Long clips are the hardest to fit. Trim the GIF to the loop you want before uploading.
A still banner works the same way: drop a PNG or JPG instead.

pages.heading: Compress a GIF for Discord: under 20 MB
pages.title: Discord message upload
pages.description: Compress a GIF to under 20 MB, Discord's upload limit without Nitro, still animated at its own size. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Without Nitro, Discord takes files up to 20 MB in a message. A GIF over that is compressed to the largest file under 20 MB, still animated, at its own pixel size.

guide.title: Getting a GIF under Discord's upload limit
paragraphs: Discord's File Attachments FAQ says that as of August 2026 the upload limit without Nitro is 20 MB, up from 10 MB. Nitro Basic raises it to 50 MB, and Nitro to up to 1 GB.

This page compresses the GIF to the largest file under 20 MB. It first tries fewer colours and gentle lossy compression; for bigger cuts it scales the frames down and, as a last step, drops some frames and holds the rest longer, so it plays at the same speed. Frame timing and looping are kept, and the result says if frames were dropped.
tips: Discord checks the size before it compresses anything, so the file you upload is the size that counts.
With Nitro Basic, pick 50 MB on the slider instead.
To make the GIF smaller in pixels too, open Exact size in pixels and enter a width and height.

pages.heading: Compress a GIF to 500 KB
pages.description: Shrink an animated GIF to under 500 KB for forum posts, profile pictures and chat. Still animated. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: A short reaction GIF saved from a video is often several MB. To reach 500 KB it is compressed and usually made smaller in pixels, and it stays a GIF that plays at its own speed.

guide.title: Getting a GIF under 500 KB
paragraphs: 500 KB is a tight limit for a GIF, because a GIF stores every frame as its own picture. A two-second loop at a few hundred pixels wide can fit; a long clip at full size cannot.

After a lossless cleanup we try lossy compression at full size, then fewer colours together with fewer pixels. Only if that is still too big are frames dropped, and the frames that stay are held longer, so it plays at the same speed. The result says if frames were dropped.
tips: Trim the GIF to the part that loops before you upload it. Fewer frames is the biggest saving there is.
Small GIFs with flat colours, like stickers and pixel art, fit far more easily than clips cut from video.
If the result is too small in pixels for you, a shorter clip will fit at a larger size.

pages.heading: Compress a GIF to 1 MB
pages.description: Shrink an animated GIF to under 1 MB for chat apps, forums and email. Still animated. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Many places that take GIFs cap them around 1 MB. A GIF over that is compressed to the largest file under 1 MB, and it keeps its frame timing and loop.

guide.title: Getting a GIF under 1 MB
paragraphs: At 1 MB a few seconds of animation usually fits, often at a smaller size in pixels. Every frame keeps its own timing, the loop setting is kept, and see-through areas stay see-through.

The steps go from gentlest to strongest: lossy compression at full size, then fewer colours and fewer pixels, and as a last resort dropping every other frame. We keep the first step that fits, so the file is as good as 1 MB allows.
tips: Check the result at the size it will be shown. A GIF made smaller in pixels can look fine in a chat window and soft when enlarged.
Screen recordings shrink much better than camera footage, because little changes from one frame to the next.
A GIF already under 1 MB is only cleaned up without visible changes; nothing is made worse to save a few more KB.

pages.heading: Compress a GIF to 2 MB
pages.description: Shrink an animated GIF to under 2 MB for websites, docs and messages. Still animated. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: A GIF made from a screen recording or a video clip is often 5 to 20 MB. To reach 2 MB it is compressed and made smaller in pixels as far as needed, and frames are dropped only as a last resort.

guide.title: Getting a GIF under 2 MB
paragraphs: The first lossy step adds a little grain that is hard to see in motion. If that is not enough, the GIF uses fewer colours and fewer pixels, a step at a time, and we keep the first step that fits. Dropping frames comes last, after the pixel size.
The GIF is never converted to a video or another format. It comes back as a GIF, with its frame delays and loop count as they were.
tips: For a GIF in documentation or a README, crop away empty parts of the screen before recording. Pixels you do not record cost nothing.
Lower the frame rate in your screen recorder if you can: 10 to 15 frames a second is usually smooth enough for a demo.
If one GIF has to carry a long demo, splitting it into two shorter GIFs keeps both sharper.

pages.heading: Compress a GIF to 5 MB
pages.description: Shrink an animated GIF to under 5 MB, keeping its size and every frame where possible. Still animated. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Long screen recordings and high-resolution clips saved as GIF can reach 20 to 50 MB. They are compressed to the largest file under 5 MB, still a GIF, with every frame kept wherever the size allows.

guide.title: Getting a GIF under 5 MB
paragraphs: Lossy compression comes first: it lets each frame differ very slightly from the original in return for a much smaller file, which is hard to notice while the GIF plays. Clips cut from video usually also need fewer pixels to reach 5 MB.
Very long or very large GIFs can still need fewer pixels. A GIF of many hundreds of frames at full HD is a lot of pictures. If frames had to be dropped, the result says so.
tips: If the GIF came from a video converter, check its frame rate. 30 or more frames a second makes a GIF large; 15 to 20 looks almost the same.
GIFs over 200 million pixels across all frames are refused rather than left running for minutes. Trim or shrink them first.
A GIF already under 5 MB is only cleaned up, losslessly.

pages.heading: Compress a GIF to 10 MB
pages.description: Shrink a large animated GIF to under 10 MB with the gentlest compression that fits. Still animated. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: A GIF over 10 MB is usually a long or high-resolution clip. It is cleaned up, then compressed, and made smaller in pixels only as far as 10 MB needs.

guide.title: Getting a GIF under 10 MB
paragraphs: Many large GIFs are bigger than they need to be: GIF makers often store each frame in full when only part of the picture changed. The first step rewrites each frame as only what changed, which changes nothing you can see and is sometimes enough on its own.
If not, gentle lossy compression follows, still at full size and with every frame. Fewer pixels or dropped frames come only after that, and only if 10 MB needs them.
tips: The original is deleted minutes after compression, and the result shortly after, so download it straight away.
Upload limits apply to the file you upload, so check the size shown on the result before you post it.
For a GIF far over 10 MB, like 50 MB or more, a shorter clip will keep more quality than squeezing the whole one.

faq.a: Yes. There is no sign-up and no watermark.

It is processed on our server and deleted automatically: the original 5 minutes after the run finishes, the compressed file after 10. A file you upload but never compress is deleted within 30 minutes. You can also delete everything right away with Delete now.
We try a lossless cleanup first, which does not change how the file looks. Only if that is not enough do we lower image quality, and we pick the gentlest setting that still fits your size.

faq.q: What if my file cannot get that small?
faq.a: You get the smallest version we could make and a clear note saying so, instead of a file that silently misses the limit.

faq.q: Why is my file a little under the limit I picked?
faq.a: Some sites count a kilobyte as 1000 bytes and others as 1024. We aim under the stricter one, so a 200 KB page aims for 200,000 bytes and the file passes either way.
